headline: OpenAI in talks to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation
body: OpenAI is in talks with investors to raise at least $30 billion in a pre-IPO round at a roughly $1.4 trillion valuation, Bloomberg reported. That would follow its $122 billion round in March at an $852 billion valuation, with run-rate revenue up 70% since July to $40 billion in August, per the report. CEO Sam Altman has ruled out a public listing in 2026 to prioritize AI safety.
note: OpenAI's March raise was meant to be its last private round before an IPO, so a bridge round at a higher price keeps its valuation untested by public markets for longer. With a listing now ruled out for 2026, private investors carry that risk into next year.

evidence.text: OpenAI is in talks with investors to raise at least $30 billion in a pre-IPO funding round at a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday.
The company previously raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion valuation.

While Anthropic momentarily outpaced OpenAI at the start of the year, recent strategic refocus on key areas like coding has fueled a 70% jump in run-rate revenue since July, reaching $40 billion in August, according to the report.
However, CEO Sam Altman has now ruled out a public debut in 2026 to prioritize AI safety first.
That funding round was supposed to be its last private raise before an IPO, which had been, until recently, expected to take place this year.
The new fundraising, if it transpires, will serve as a bridge round to the IPO, according to Bloomberg.
Investors are eager to pour more funds into the ChatGPT maker ahead of its anticipated public market debut next year.

correction: An earlier version said OpenAI had delayed its IPO again and claimed to know what analysts watch most closely. The source reports one change of timing, from this year to next, and says nothing about analysts.
